	<body>
		<segment id="1" parent="77" relname="span">According to 17 U . S . C . § 504 ( c ) , a plaintiff in an action for copyright infringement shall be entitled to statutory damages of " not less than $ 750 or more than $ 30,000 " for " all infringements</segment>
		<segment id="2" parent="1" relname="elaboration">involved in the action ,</segment>
		<segment id="3" parent="78" relname="span">with respect to any one work ,</segment>
		<segment id="4" parent="3" relname="mode">as the court considers just . "</segment>
		<segment id="5" parent="79" relname="explanation">17 U . S . C . § 504 ( c ) ( 1 ) .</segment>
		<segment id="6" parent="82" relname="same-unit">However ,</segment>
		<segment id="7" parent="8" relname="contingency">if the infringement is deemed to have been committed " willfully , "</segment>
		<segment id="8" parent="81" relname="span">the court may increase the award of statutory damages up to a sum of $ 150,000 per infringed work .</segment>
		<segment id="9" parent="82" relname="explanation">17 U . S . C . § 504 ( c ) ( 2 ) .</segment>
		<segment id="10" parent="85" relname="span">" Statutory damages for copyright infringement are available</segment>
		<segment id="11" parent="10" relname="mode">without proof of plaintiff ' s actual damages or proof of any damages . "</segment>
		<segment id="12" parent="86" relname="span">All - Star Mktg . Group , LLC v . Media Brands Co .. , 775 F . Supp . 2 d 613, 626</segment>
		<segment id="13" parent="12" relname="elaboration">( S . D . N . Y . 2011 )</segment>
		<segment id="14" parent="86" relname="adversative">( internal quotations omitted ) .</segment>
		<segment id="15" parent="16" relname="context">When determining the appropriate amount of statutory damages ,</segment>
		<segment id="16" parent="90" relname="span">the Court considers the following six factors :</segment>
		<segment id="17" parent="100" relname="joint">( 1 ) the infringer ' s state of mind ;</segment>
		<segment id="18" parent="92" relname="span">( 2 ) the expenses</segment>
		<segment id="19" parent="91" relname="span">saved , and profits</segment>
		<segment id="20" parent="19" relname="elaboration">earned , by the infringer ;</segment>
		<segment id="21" parent="93" relname="span">( 3 ) the revenues</segment>
		<segment id="22" parent="21" relname="elaboration">lost by the copyright holder ;</segment>
		<segment id="23" parent="97" relname="joint">( 4 ) the deterrent effect on the infringer and third parties ;</segment>
		<segment id="24" parent="95" relname="span">( 5 ) the infringer ' s cooperation</segment>
		<segment id="25" parent="94" relname="span">in providing evidence</segment>
		<segment id="26" parent="25" relname="elaboration">concerning the value of the infringing material ;</segment>
		<segment id="27" parent="96" relname="joint">and ( 6 ) the conduct and attitude of the parties .</segment>
		<segment id="28" parent="102" relname="span">Bryant v . Media Right Prods . , Inc . , 603 F . 3 d 135, 144</segment>
		<segment id="29" parent="28" relname="context">( 2 d Cir . 2010 ) .</segment>
		<segment id="30" parent="108" relname="span">Here , factors 1 and 6 weigh heavily in favor of Plaintiff</segment>
		<segment id="31" parent="107" relname="span">because Defendants knew of the infringing activity</segment>
		<segment id="32" parent="104" relname="span">by not only intentionally designing their websites</segment>
		<segment id="33" parent="32" relname="purpose">to do so ,</segment>
		<segment id="34" parent="105" relname="span">but by frequently distorting , blocking , or otherwise making un - viewable the copyright notices</segment>
		<segment id="35" parent="34" relname="elaboration">that Plaintiff had originally built into the web - page .</segment>
		<segment id="36" parent="110" relname="span">Factor 5 also weighs heavily in favor of Plaintiff due to the failure of the Defendants to appear ,</segment>
		<segment id="37" parent="109" relname="span">which has limited the information</segment>
		<segment id="38" parent="37" relname="elaboration">that could have further been discovered by Plaintiff .</segment>
		<segment id="39" parent="115" relname="span">As for factors 2, 3 and 4 , Defendants have been able to save the expenses</segment>
		<segment id="40" parent="114" relname="span">that they would have incurred</segment>
		<segment id="41" parent="113" relname="joint">in designing a website</segment>
		<segment id="42" parent="112" relname="span">and / or to properly purchasing a license from Plaintiff</segment>
		<segment id="43" parent="42" relname="purpose">to use the websites .</segment>
		<segment id="44" parent="117" relname="span">In addition , the infringement has cost Plaintiff valuable rankings in search engines</segment>
		<segment id="45" parent="44" relname="evaluation">( which can determine the success of a business ) ;</segment>
		<segment id="46" parent="119" relname="span">Defendants have diverted potential customers from Plaintiff ' s sites ,</segment>
		<segment id="47" parent="118" relname="span">who otherwise would have access to the sites</segment>
		<segment id="48" parent="47" relname="contingency">if it were not for Defendants infringement .</segment>
		<segment id="49" parent="123" relname="same-unit">Moreover ,</segment>
		<segment id="50" parent="51" relname="causal">because actual damages would be hard to prove ,</segment>
		<segment id="51" parent="122" relname="span">statutory damages are appropriate .</segment>
		<segment id="52" parent="124" relname="elaboration">Plaintiff is seeking statutory damages in the amount of $ 150,000 .</segment>
		<segment id="53" parent="129" relname="purpose">To prove " willfulness " under the Copyright Act ,</segment>
		<segment id="54" parent="128" relname="attribution">the plaintiff must show</segment>
		<segment id="55" parent="128" relname="joint">( 1 ) that the defendant was actually aware of the infringing activity ,</segment>
		<segment id="56" parent="128" relname="joint">or ( 2 ) that the defendant ' s actions were the result of " reckless disregard " for , or " willful blindness " to , the copyright holder ' s rights .</segment>
		<segment id="57" parent="131" relname="span">Island Software and Comp . Serv . , Inc . v . Microsoft Corp . , 413 F . 3 d 257, 262</segment>
		<segment id="58" parent="57" relname="context">( 2 d Cir . 2005 )</segment>
		<segment id="59" parent="132" relname="span">( where defendant recklessly disregarded the possibility</segment>
		<segment id="60" parent="59" relname="elaboration">that its conduct represented infringement ) .</segment>
		<segment id="61" parent="134" relname="span">Here , Defendants took the time</segment>
		<segment id="62" parent="61" relname="purpose">to cover over the copyright notices on Plaintiff ' s website .</segment>
		<segment id="63" parent="138" relname="attribution">Defendants should also know</segment>
		<segment id="64" parent="136" relname="span">that their software</segment>
		<segment id="65" parent="135" relname="span">— which was designed</segment>
		<segment id="66" parent="65" relname="purpose">to copy other websites —</segment>
		<segment id="67" parent="137" relname="span">would be infringing the copyrights and trademarks</segment>
		<segment id="68" parent="67" relname="elaboration">that are owned by those websites .</segment>
		<segment id="69" parent="142" relname="span">The statutory damages in the present case are appropriate</segment>
		<segment id="70" parent="69" relname="causal">due to the willful and egregious disregard by the Defendants and their actions .</segment>
		<segment id="71" parent="143" relname="span">This should also serve as a deterrent not only to the current Defendant , but as a general deterrent to others</segment>
		<segment id="72" parent="71" relname="elaboration">who may contemplate engaging in this " fake hack " infringing behavior in the future .</segment>
		<segment id="73" parent="148" relname="joint">All - Star Mktg .</segment>
		<segment id="74" parent="147" relname="joint">Grp . , 775 F .</segment>
		<segment id="75" parent="147" relname="joint">Supp . 2 d at 627 .</segment>

</rst>']}, {'index': 7, 'label': 'Analysis of Attorneys’ Fees', 'content': 'The District Court in its discretion may award reasonable attorney's fee to the prevailing party in a copyright infringement action. See  17 U.S.C. § 505 ;  Bryant, 603 F.3d at 144 . Generally, in deciding whether to make such an award, the Court considers the following four factors: (1) the frivolousness of the losing party's claims or defenses; (2) the losing party's motivation; (3) whether the claims or defenses were objectively unreasonable; and (4) compensation and deterrence. See id . The third factor, objective unreasonableness of the claims or defenses, is given substantial weight. See id . Here, Plaintiff's submission and the default by Defendants establish the frivolousness and objective unreasonableness of the defense under factors 1 and 3. Regarding Defendants' motivation, factor 2, the Court has concluded that Defendants did not act in good faith in defending the action, but rather engaged in a strategy of noncompliance and delay. A large number of the hours expended by Plaintiff's counsel was due to the noncompliance of the Defendants. Under these circumstances, an award of attorney's fees is warranted as compensation to Plaintiff and as a future deterrent against this conduct on the part of Defendants and other infringers.
